inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: Harry Wait was found guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge after requesting ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent, though he was acquitted of another identity theft count. His claim that he was exposing vulnerabilities doesn’t excuse manufacturing fraud—but neither does this case justify making voting harder for ordinary people. The real danger is turning isolated misconduct into an excuse to undermine public trust or restrict access. We need election systems that are both secure and accessible, and accountability that protects voters rather than punishing them.
